newsitem.title: MALI: Mali shuts schools, warns opponents in poll run-up.
newsitem.headline: Mali shuts schools, warns opponents in poll run-up.

text.p: Mali on Wednesday ordered schools to close for a week and said student demonstrations had been planned with opposition politicians to sow disorder in the run-up to Sunday's presidential election.

"There was a meeting between students and opposition leaders. They adopted a scenario to create a situation ripe for insurrection during which blood would flow," government spokesman Bakare Konimba Traore said in a televised statement.

Security forces on Tuesday fired teargas to clear students who threw stones and burned campaign posters of President Alpha Oumar Konare, who stands for re-election on Sunday in a contentious election.

The multi-party presidential poll is the impoverished West African country's second since independence from France in 1960 and seen as a key test of democracy, but opposition parties have called for a boycott.

The students, who are protesting against a slow and chaotic start to the school year, also want the departure of Konare -- whose insistence on keeping a May 11 date for the presidential poll outraged opposition supporters.

"The government will prevent anyone who wants to come to power by other means than the ballot box," Traore said. He added that schools and colleges would be shut until Tuesday to ensure that children did not get hurt.

Representatives of 15 non-political interest groups, among them the main Islamic body, unions and the business association, condemned both government and opposition politicians for failing to reach an agreement on holding the election.
"We ask the political class to weigh up the consequences of such behaviour," a joint statement from the groups said.
Konare's only challenger is businessman Hamadou Maribatrou Diaby.

Political analysts in Bamako compare the current wave of student demonstrations and power and water workers' strikes with the tension which gripped the city before the 1991 overthrow of former one-party ruler General Moussa Traore by the military.
